Faizan --Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand --Respondent
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Mohd. Safdar, learned counsel for the
applicant.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. for the
State.
3. By means of the present Anticipatory Bail
Application, the applicant is seeking anticipatory
bail in Case Crime No.349 of 2026, under
Sections 3, 5, 11 of Uttarakhand Protection for
Cow Progeny Act, 2007, Police Station Kotwali
Ranipur, District Haridwar.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant, while
drawing the attention of the Court to the FIR,
would submit that the applicant has no concern
with the alleged recovery and that no arrest was
made at the spot. He would further submit that
there is a delay of approximately 51⁄2 hours in
lodging the FIR.
5. He would further submit that a perusal of
the FIR reveals that the applicant has been
named therein solely on the basis of the
statement of co-accused Waseem. Except for the
statement of the co-accused, there is no other
evidence against the applicant.
6. Per contra, learned State counsel would
submit that the name of the applicant was

disclosed by the arrested accused.
7. Learned State counsel would further submit
that the case of applicant Faizan is slightly
different from that of applicant Mursaleen,
inasmuch as cow slaughter is alleged to have
taken place at the residence of applicant Faizan.
However, a bare perusal of the FIR reveals that no
bloodstains were found at the residence of the
applicant. There is only one allegation in the FIR
that, while the accused persons were escaping
after the cow slaughter, one of the co-accused
was found in the courtyard.
8. He has also drawn the attention of the
Court to the order dated 03.11.2026 passed by
the learned District and Sessions Judge,
Haridwar, rejecting the applicant's anticipatory
bail application. He would further submit that
two other cases of a similar nature (Case Crime
Nos.264 of 2017 and 17 of 2025) are registered
against the applicant.
9. On this, learned counsel for the applicant
would submit that the applicant is already on bail
in the aforesaid two cases.
10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties
and upon perusal of the record, it is apparent
that the applicant has been implicated merely on
the basis of the disclosure made by the co-accused. No recovery has been effected from the
applicant, nor was he arrested at the spot.
Further, the applicant is already on bail in the
aforesaid two cases.
11. Having considered the submissions
advanced by learned counsel for the parties, but

without expressing any opinion on the final
merits of the case, this Court is of the view that
the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on
anticipatory bail. Accordingly, the anticipatory
bail application deserves to be allowed.
12. The Anticipatory Bail Application is allowed.
13. In the eventuality of arrest, the applicant
shall be enlarged on bail on his furnishing a
personal bond in the sum of Rs.20,000/- with
two sureties, each in the like amount, to the
satisfaction of the Investigating Officer ("IO"). In
addition to it, the applicant shall also comply with
the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall co-operate with the
investigation.
(ii) The applicant shall not approach any
witness/victim in any manner, whatsoever.
(iii)The applicant shall not leave the country
without prior permission of the concerned
court.
(iv) The applicant shall deposit his passport
with the Investigating Officer ("IO"). The
passport may only be returned by the order of
the court concerned. In case the applicant does
not have passport, he shall give an undertaking
to that effect to the IO.
(v) The applicant shall also give an undertaking
on (i), (ii) & (iii) above.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.)
 06-11-2026
Akash
